title: ISO/IEC 17025
shortDescription: The standard behind every NABL-accredited testing and calibration laboratory — competence, impartiality, and the general requirements every non-medical lab is assessed against.
genZNote: If a lab tests materials, products, or measures things (not human specimens), this is its standard.

sections.heading: Purpose and Scope
sections.body: ISO/IEC 17025, ‘General requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories’, is the international standard accreditation bodies (including NABL) use to accredit testing and calibration laboratories — everything from chemical/material testing to instrument calibration, excluding medical laboratories (which use ISO 15189 instead). The current edition is ISO/IEC 17025:2017.

sections.heading: Core Requirements
bullets: Competence — personnel, methods, and equipment demonstrably capable of producing valid results.
Impartiality — the lab's results and judgements must not be influenced by commercial or other pressure.
Confidentiality — client information and results are protected.
Resources — suitable personnel, facilities, equipment, and environmental conditions.
Methods — validated/verified test and calibration methods, appropriately selected for the work.
Sampling and handling of test/calibration items — controlled from receipt to disposal.
Technical records and reporting — records that allow a result to be reconstructed, and reports that meet defined content requirements.
Quality management, nonconforming work, corrective action, internal audits, management review, and continual improvement — the same closed-loop cycle used throughout this subject.

rows: Adds clinical/patient-centred requirements (consent, critical results, clinical advice)
General competence requirements, no clinical/patient dimension

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: ISO/IEC 17025 is the international standard for the general competence of testing and calibration laboratories — the standard NABL uses for non-medical labs. Current edition: 2017.
keyFacts: Covers testing laboratories AND calibration laboratories under one standard.
Impartiality and confidentiality are explicit, named requirements — not just implied good practice.
ISO 15189's 2022 structure was deliberately aligned to match ISO/IEC 17025:2017's format.
commonConfusion: A calibration lab and a testing lab are both accredited under the SAME standard (ISO/IEC 17025) — they are two NABL programmes sharing one standard, not two different standards.

highYieldFacts: Impartiality and confidentiality are standalone named requirements in this standard.
Testing labs and calibration labs share this one standard — the split is by NABL programme, not by ISO standard.
commonTraps: Applying ISO/IEC 17025 to a medical/diagnostic laboratory — that's ISO 15189's territory.
Assuming testing and calibration labs need different standards — they don't.
mustRemember: ISO/IEC 17025 → testing and calibration labs (non-medical). ISO 15189 → medical labs.

confusedTerms.distinction: Both are accredited under ISO/IEC 17025. Testing labs determine properties of a sample/product; calibration labs establish the accuracy of measuring instruments against traceable references.
